affected.description:
Every check this alert speaks for, the first being [`Self::check`]. More

kind.description: What kind of event it is, shared by every instance of it.

What to do about it, most likely first. An alert that says what happened

severity.description:
How much it matters. A resolution takes the severity of what resolved,

Criticality.description:
How much a service's absence costs.

Serialisable as well as readable, because it reaches an operator: a status
report that says a service is down without saying whether that matters
leaves them to guess, and the manifest already holds the answer.

oneOf.description: Its failure has consequences outside the machine.
The form does not work without it.
The form works, badly.
Makes things better.

Hardlink.description:
Whether imports are hardlinking or copying — the difference between an import
that is free and one that doubles the disk it uses.

oneOf.description: Imports hardlink, as they should.
Imports copy, doubling space and slowing every import.
It could not be established which.

Moment.description:
Which way a condition went.

Both directions are worth saying and neither is worth saying twice. An operator
told a disk filled up and never told it was resolved goes on believing it — so
resolution is an alert in its own right rather than the absence of one.

oneOf.description: It started.

Panel.description:
A panel's content, or the reason its source could not fill it.

The difference between "this panel is up to date" and "this panel's source is
unreachable" is the whole of degrading honestly: an unavailable panel says so,
in its own words, rather than showing stale data as current or blank data as
zero — and the panels beside it stay live.

Protocol.description:
Which protocol a transfer is moving over, since the same download reads
differently on each — a Usenet download has no peers, a torrent has no server.

A torrent download.

Queue.description: One `*arr`'s queue, and how much of it is stuck.

service.description: The service whose queue this is.

stuck.description: How many of them are stuck rather than progressing.

Reading.description:
A figure a source reports, kept apart from the two ways it can be missing.

Zero is a value a source gave; stale is the last value a source that has since
gone quiet gave; unknown is a source that never answered at all. Collapsing any
two of them sends an operator after the wrong problem — a stalled download and
a dashboard that simply stopped polling look identical only if the code lets
them.

oneOf.description:
The source answered this refresh with a value — which may legitimately be
zero.
The source did not answer this refresh; this is the last value it gave.
The source has never answered, so nothing can be said about it.

criticality.description: How much its absence costs, so a summary can weigh it.

depends_on.description:
The services it needs before it can work, as the manifest declares them.
Carried so a failure can be attributed to the thing underneath it rather
than counted as one more independent thing wrong.

exit.description: How it exited, where it has exited.

id.description: The service's identifier, which is also its Compose service name.

name.description: What it is called in front of an operator.

Severity.description:
How much a problem matters.

Four levels, deliberately. More would not be applied consistently, and
inconsistent severity is worse than coarse severity.

oneOf.description: Informational; nothing is required.
Degraded or risky, still working.
Something is broken.
Consequences outside the machine, or data at risk.

Snapshot.description:
Everything the dashboard shows at one moment.

Each source's panel is filled or marked unavailable on its own, so one dead
source degrades one region rather than the screen. The surface builds this from
what it gathered; the standing is read from the same facts so it cannot
disagree with the panels.

alerts.description:
What the operator has been told, newest first: what is owed them where a
channel is refusing, then what has already been said.

health.description:
The one-line health summary — the same computation every other surface
uses, so no two of them can grade the same stack differently.

Always present, unlike the panels: a stack that could not be reached has a
summary, and it says `unknown`. An absent summary would leave the operator
to infer health from a blank space, which is the one reading this must never
be open to.

services.description: Every service and what it is doing.

stuck.description:
What in the pipeline has stopped, worst first — assessed across the
download clients and the \*arrs together, because the failure that matters
most is invisible inside either.

telemetry.description: Whether the screen itself can be trusted to be current.

vpn.description:
The VPN, or `None` where no VPN is configured and the panel is omitted
rather than shown permanently red.

Stall.description:
Why an item is not moving.

Ordered by how much of the operator's attention each deserves, worst first, so
a summary that leads with the worst category needs no second ranking.

oneOf.description:
Fetched over and over: import is failing silently and being retried, which
spends bandwidth and Usenet allowance indefinitely while looking normal.

The same item has failed to import more than once. Structural — it will not
resolve itself.

Downloaded successfully and never imported. The failure nobody owns: the
client considers it finished, the \*arr never picked it up, and from each
service's own perspective there is nothing wrong.
On disk, and no \*arr knows about it.
No progress at all beyond the threshold.

Monitored, never grabbed — nothing matched, or the indexers are answering
with nothing.

Moving, but slowly enough to be worth knowing about. Deliberately its own
category rather than a stall: something still arriving needs patience, not
intervention, and reporting the two alike is how a queue check gets muted.

Standing.description:
What the stack amounts to.

Ordered from best to worst, so the worst of several is a `max` and there is no
second place to encode the ranking.

oneOf.description: Nothing is wrong.
Nothing is running, and that was on purpose.
Nothing is set up.
Worth knowing, nothing to do.
Working, with something wrong.
Something is broken.
Something is wrong outside this machine, or data is at risk.
It could not be established. Never reported as healthy.

State.description:
What one service is actually doing.

Ordered from worst to best, so a form's condition is the minimum across its
services and needs no comparison table. The declaration order is therefore
load-bearing.

oneOf.description: Exited without being asked to, and is not coming back on its own.
Exiting and restarting repeatedly.
Running, and its own probe says it is not working.
No container exists.
A container exists and is not running.
Running, and still inside its probe's start period.

Running, and declaring no probe by which to know more.

Distinct from healthy on purpose. A service that cannot be asked is not
a service that answered, and rendering the two identically is how a
dashboard comes to be believed about something it never checked.
Running and passing its own probe.
The operating system owns this one, not lemonfiber.

Storage.description: The storage picture: what is free, when it runs out, and whether imports link.

exhaustion.description:
The time until the disk fills at the current rate of the queue draining
onto it, or `None` where it is not projected to fill.

free.description:
Bytes free on the data volume — a [`Reading`], since a volume that could
not be read this refresh must not render as zero free.

hardlink.description: Whether imports are linking or copying.

Stuck.description: One thing that is wrong, and why.

blocking.description:
What the service said was blocking it, in its own words, where it said
anything. A permission denial from an import log is worth more than any
interpretation of it, and it is the difference between "stuck" and
something an operator can fix.

held_for.description:
How long it has been that way, in seconds — what turns "stuck" into a
sentence an operator can weigh.

items.description:
How many items this stands for. One in the ordinary case; more where they
share a cause and the cause is what is wrong — twenty downloads stopped by
a full disk are one thing to fix, and twenty alerts about it are how an
operator learns to mute the queue check.

name.description: Which item — or, where several share one cause, that cause.

Summary.description: The one-line summary, and what it expands to.

affected.description:
Everything that is wrong, worst first, so the line expands to the affected
items and their remedies rather than to a number nobody can act on.

wanting_attention.description:
How many things are wrong — root causes, counted once each, so a disk that
filled and the nine imports that then failed is one thing and not ten.

worst.description:
The worst thing, named, so the line says something rather than only
grading. Absent where nothing is wrong.

Telemetry.description:
How the screen itself is doing, which is a different question from how the
stack is doing.

The stack's own verdict is [`crate::health::Standing`]; this is only whether the
picture can be trusted to be current. Kept apart because they disagree in both
directions: a healthy stack can be shown through half-failing telemetry, and a
perfectly refreshing screen can be reporting a stack that is on fire.

oneOf.description: Telemetry is current and refreshing normally.
Some sources are unavailable; their panels are marked.
The engine cannot be reached, though the CLI path may still work.
Configured, but nothing is running.
No configuration; setup is offered instead.

Transfer.description: One active download, as the dashboard shows it.

eta.description: The time left, or `None` where it is stalled and there is none to give.

progress.description: How far along, as a percentage from zero to a hundred.

speed.description:
The current speed in bytes per second — a [`Reading`], because a genuine
zero (stalled) and a source that has gone quiet mean opposite things here,
and this is the very figure that difference is about.

Vpn.description: What the VPN is doing, and whether the download client is actually behind it.

country.description: The country that address is in.

egress_matches.description:

exit_ip.description: The tunnel's exit address as the outside world sees it.

forwarded_port.description: The port the provider forwards, where forwarding is on.

Code.description:
A stable identifier for a kind of problem.

Stability is the whole point: an operator who searches for a code should find
the same answer a year later. Codes are declared as constants beside the code
that raises them, and are never recycled.

LogLine.description:
One line of output from one service.

Serialisable because a log stream is part of the machine-readable contract:
`--json` renders one envelope per line, since a stream has no last element
to close a document with.

at.description:
When the container itself says it wrote the line, where it said so.

Kept verbatim and unparsed. Containers disagree with the host clock and
with each other, and the only defensible ordering is each container's own
account of itself — which a reader can only apply if it is carried
rather than replaced by an arrival time.

line.description: The line, without its trailing newline.

service.description: The Compose service it came from.

Stream.description: Which stream a log line arrived on.

oneOf.description: Standard output.
Standard error.

setup.description: The wrapper every machine-readable payload arrives in.

kind.description: Which payload this is, so a consumer can branch before parsing `data`.

Protocols.description:
Which download protocols the operator actually has accounts for.

A form names both, because a form describes what it *does* rather than what
this operator has paid for. Narrowing happens afterwards, so a tunnel is
never started with credentials that were never supplied.

torrent.description: A VPN and torrent client are configured.

oneOf.description: The reviewed answers were written.
The plan was seen and not applied; nothing was written.
Nothing was asked, because this machine was already set up.

SetupReport.description:
What a setup run came to, and what it settled on.

**Deliberately not the settings themselves.** Setup writes an indexer key and a
service password among them, and a report a script can read is a report a script
can log — into a file, a CI transcript, somebody's terminal history. So this says
what was *decided* and never what was *entered*, and the fields are chosen one at
a time rather than by serialising a struct that might later gain a secret.

The indexer's address is left out for that reason rather than because it is
itself a secret: it is entered beside its key, and the two travel together in
every place an operator copies them from.

data_root.description: Where the library was put, where a location was chosen.

protocols.description: Which ways of downloading the stack was set up for.

service_user.description: The user the services run as, as `uid:gid`, where one was set.

kind.description: Which payload this is, so a consumer can branch before parsing `data`.

next.description: What to do next, in order.

Line.description: One narrated line: a step, and what was specifically true of it.

detail.description:
What was specifically true — the evidence that makes the line worth reading
rather than a spinner. Empty where there is nothing particular to say.

said.description: What it is doing, in plain language.

Link.description:
What the import did with the finished download — the difference between one copy of a
file and two.

oneOf.description:
The library entry and the download are the same file under two names, which is
what a correctly-shared volume allows and what costs no extra disk.

The file was copied, so it now exists twice. Works, but every import costs its own
size again and seeding a torrent holds the second copy for as long as it seeds.
Add more content, now that the shape of it is understood.
Let the rest of the household ask for things themselves.
Watch it somewhere other than the machine it is running on.

Reason.description: Why a walkthrough could not go on.

oneOf.description:
No indexer is configured, so there is nothing to search. Not a failure of the
walk — a reason not to offer it at all.

The search could not be run: the indexers, or the service holding them, would not
answer.

The search ran cleanly and matched nothing. An entirely different problem from
the one above, and the one operators most often mistake for it.

Releases exist, but none meets the chosen quality preset. The stack is working;
the preset and what is out there disagree.
Torrents are in play and the tunnel is not verified up. Nothing is grabbed.
The release was never handed to a download client.
The download stopped making progress.
The download finished and the library manager would not take it.
There is no media server in the running form to make it playable.
It was imported, the media server was told, and it still cannot be found there.

Shape.description: Which walkthrough this stack is offered.

oneOf.description: The full walk: search, grab, download, import, and see it in the library.

The walk for a stack that acquires nothing: point at media already on disk and
confirm the media server can see it.

State.description: What has become of a walkthrough.

oneOf.description: Presented at the end of setup, not yet answered.

Declined. Available later, and carrying no penalty — a stack that was set up is

Looking for releases.
Sending a release to the download client.
The download is running.
Moving the finished download into the library.
It is in the library and playable.
Stopped at a named step, with a diagnosis.
The operator left part-way. Whatever was in flight stays in flight.

Step.description: One step of the walk, ordered from picking something to watching it play.

oneOf.description: Picking something to add, and confirming it is not already here.
The indexers are being searched for releases.
A release is being sent to the download client.
The download is running.
The \*arr is moving the finished download into the library.
The media server is being told to look at what arrived.

Stopped.description: A walkthrough that stopped: where, why, what the services were saying, and what to do.

logs.description:
What the services involved were saying at the time, shown inline rather than left
for the operator to go and find — a fault report they have to research is a fault
report they abandon.

WalkthroughReport.description:
What a first-content walkthrough did — the whole of it, narrated line by line as it
happened and gathered here so the ending can be rendered, serialised and exited on.

already_here.description: Whether what was asked for was already here, and so was not acquired again.

handover.description: Where it leaves the operator, where it worked.

in_background.description: Whether the download was handed to the background rather than waited out.

item.description: What it walked, where it got as far as choosing something.

lines.description:
Every line it said, in order — the same lines the operator watched arrive, kept so
a machine-readable run is not a silent one.

link.description: What the import did with the file, where it got that far.

proves.description: What it set out to prove, said so the operator knows what they watched.

stopped.description: Where and why it stopped, where it did.

suggestions.description:
What could have been walked instead, where nothing was chosen — the safe first

kind.description: Which payload this is, so a consumer can branch before parsing `data`.

Term.description: A word this product uses, and what somebody meeting it needs to know.

also_called.description:
What other services in this stack call the same thing.

Sonarr and `SABnzbd` do not agree on words, and an operator moving between
their screens should not have to work out that two of them are one.

deep.description: More, for somebody who asks — never needed in order to act.

short.description:
One sentence: what it is for and what it costs or gains.

Enough to act on. Somebody who reads only this should not be stuck.
